body: Wednesday, March 19 2025 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information available before 2025-03-19 00:00 UTC. Prices use completed prior sessions. Prepared retrospectively; later outcomes are excluded.

Macro Stance: Wall Street is in a correction rather than a crash, and the Fed meets into it. The S&P 500 closed at 5,614.66 on 18 March, down 8.40% over 20 sessions, while the Nasdaq 100 is 12.10% lower over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Reuters reported Bank of America’s survey showing the biggest drop in US equity allocation on record, which the bank calls a ‘bull crash’ [1]. Business Insider reports that investors have dumped a record amount of US stock as stagflation fears bite [2]. The growth data are softer than the inflation data. February payrolls rose by 151,000 [3], retail sales came in weaker than expected [4], and US CPI slid under consensus to 2.8% [5]. Strategists say the sell-off has ‘further to go’ as the Fed and tariff deadlines loom [6].

Rates & Curve: The curve is positively sloped. The 10-year closed at 4.29% and the 2-year at 4.04%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +25 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-18). Over 20 observations the move is bull flattening: the 2-year fell 25 bps and the 10-year fell 26 bps, so the spread narrowed by 1 bp. Over five observations the front end gave back a little ground, with the 2-year up 10 bps and the 10-year up 1 bp (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-18). The 3-month bill sits at 4.34%, keeping the 10Y−3M spread at −5 bps. The bond market is pricing a growth scare, not an inflation scare. The VIX rose 5.80% in the last session to 21.70 and is up 41.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The dollar index is at 103.24 index points, down 3.56% over 20 sessions, so the Treasury rally is not a dollar story.

New / Most Important: The decision that matters is the Fed’s on March 19. Bitcoin traders are already positioning around it, with one whale placing a $368 million short at 40x leverage ahead of the meeting [7]. Expectations had already moved toward easing, with Bloomberg reporting that the Fed is expected to cut twice this year, starting in September [8]. Options are underpricing the reaction, according to Nasdaq’s volatility note [9]. Powell is contending with what the Wall Street Journal calls a double threat of economic chaos and political hostility [10], and Trump’s nomination of Governor Michelle Bowman as vice chair for supervision adds a governance question to the meeting [11].

Playbook ✓: Own duration rather than the index. The 10-year at 4.29% has room to rally if the Fed sounds patient, and TLT at 90.71 USD is already up 2.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Trim the AI leaders into strength: the Nasdaq 100 is down 12.10% over 20 sessions and XLK is down 12.39% in the same window. Keep a hedge, because a VIX at 21.70 does not pay for complacency. The call changes if the 10-year climbs back above 4.55%, the level it held 20 observations ago, since a bond rally that fails would leave duration without protection. Rotate rather than exit: staples and utilities have held up better than discretionary, which is down 14.52% over 20 sessions.

Macro Stance: Europe is turning from restraint to spending, and the market is rewarding it. On 18 March the German parliament passed the debt-rule reform and a half-trillion-euro fund [12]. Bankier reports that the Bundestag changed the constitution and left the military budget without limits [13]. BBC reports that Germany voted for a historic boost to defence and infrastructure spending [14]. The Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 5,485.01, up 3.30% over five sessions, and the DAX is up 4.71% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). BNP Paribas says euro strength, not dollar weakness, is driving markets [15]. The ECB has already eased, cutting its key rate to 2.5% on 6 March [16], and the Bundesbank is using AI to prove the ECB’s dovish bias [17].

Credit & Inflation: Credit is quiet, but the cost of borrowing matters. France’s borrowing costs were near a 14-year high before the Fitch review [18], and Moody’s cut Romania’s outlook on budget risks [19]. The fiscal impulse runs the other way. DIW says Germany’s expansion would boost GDP from 2026 [20], and German investor morale rose sharply in March [21]. Inflation is the constraint on the ECB. Lagarde warned that trade and defence shocks risk amplifying euro-zone inflation [22], while the fall in German inflation gives the ECB more room to ease [23]. The OECD says Trump’s trade wars are slowing global growth and fuelling inflation [24].

New / Most Important: The signal that matters is that the German fiscal shift has passed parliament, not just a proposal [12]. Reuters has broken down the agreed plan [25], and DW puts the impact at €1 trillion [26]. Defence is the direct beneficiary. Rheinmetall is up 55.63% over 20 sessions and 25.26% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18), and Reuters reported it overtook Volkswagen’s market value on 13 March [27]. Reuters also reports that Europe’s top money managers are only starting to bring defence stocks in from the cold [28]. Everyone loves German rearmament, Bloomberg wrote on 17 March [29].

Playbook ✓: Own the German fiscal chain on dips, meaning industrials, infrastructure and defence, but size it for a ceasefire. Avoid the autos: the European auto ETF is down 5.10% over 20 sessions, and BMW’s annual net profit fell 37% (CNBC, 14 March) [30]. Euro strength argues for hedging dollar-earning exporters rather than the German domestic names. The call changes if Russia–Ukraine talks produce a truce that removes the defence premium [31], or if the budget fails to show up in German orders.

Macro Stance: Beijing is spending its political capital on consumption. CNBC reports the plan to ‘vigorously boost consumption’ as a bid to shore up the economy [32], SCMP counts a 30-point toolbox [33], and calls the package the most comprehensive since the 1970s [34]. Equities are responding. The Hang Seng closed at 24,740.57, up 7.68% over 20 sessions and 2.46% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The question is whether the activity data confirm the plan, and so far they only partly do. Beijing’s consumption push is also a labour story: lawmakers are targeting the job-market bias against over-35s [35].

PMIs & Activity: February’s non-manufacturing PMI was 50.4 [36]. Industrial output rose 5.9% in January and February, beating expectations [37], and retail sales were up 4% over the first two months [38]. The growth is policy-led, not private-demand-led. Reuters says retail sales are picking up as Beijing turns to consumers to ease US trade pressure [39]. Prices are the caution: consumer prices fell in February and remain flat in a sluggish economy [40]. What would confirm the view is the next official manufacturing PMI not falling, with retail sales holding up once the trade-in subsidies are working through the data.

Credit Impulse: Credit is a policy story for now. The central bank says it will create ‘more tools’ to shore up the economy [41], and Bank of China is setting up a $7 billion fund to support technology development [42]. Foreign investors are lining up for high-yielding Chinese bank debt [43]. The test is whether the tools reach households and private borrowers, rather than state banks and technology funds. Developers still need the banks: ICBC (Asia) is backing Hong Kong developers with loan support as the sector struggles [44].

Property: Property is the drag the equity rally does not price. Bloomberg reports that home prices are falling at a faster pace despite revival efforts [45], and Reuters says the slump persists as stimulus struggles to stabilise the sector [46]. Developers diverge. Sunac warns of a wider loss for 2024 [47], while Country Garden’s unit forecasts higher annual earnings [48]. China Vanke’s Hong Kong unit reports strong flat sales despite mortgage concerns [49]. Foreign funds have been selling China’s commercial properties for a fourth year, SCMP reports [50].

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal and trade policy pull in opposite directions. Beijing is doubling down on trade-ins to boost sluggish consumption [51], but the OECD finds that Trump’s tariffs will slow China’s economy and impede global trade [52]. Importers are rushing to beat the tariffs and living on the edge [53]. Trump says Xi may visit the US in the not-too-distant future [54], though analysts doubt a summit will make headway on trade [55]. Target, which relies on China for 30% of its merchandise, warned of a profit hit as the trade war bites [56]. Chinese economists are calling for a wider social safety net to nurture consumption [57].

Markets & Flows: Equities are leading the data. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,429.76 index points, up 3.17% over 20 sessions, and ASHR, the CSI 300 ETF, is at 27.60 USD, up 3.10% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). KWEB, the internet ETF, is up 6.17% over 20 sessions at 37.83 USD. USD/CNY at 7.2327 is 0.28% lower over 20 sessions, so the yuan is firming, not sliding. Reuters argues that Chinese stocks offer a hedge against fading US exceptionalism [58], and Business Insider explains why China’s stock market is roaring after investors fled in 2024 [59]. Hong Kong’s stock market is booming while Wall Street is in turmoil, Bloomberg reports [60], and China’s stock rerating is widening the premiums in the ADRs of Alibaba and Li Auto [61]. The tech leg is AI. Alibaba has revamped its Quark search engine into an AI super assistant [62], and Tencent is pushing open-source 3D generation tools [63].

New / Most Important: The new signal is the scale of the consumption push, paired with an equity market that is trading the policy rather than the property data. The plan to ‘vigorously boost consumption’ is an explicit bid to shore up growth [32], and the package is the most comprehensive in decades [34]. Tariffs are the offset. If the Hang Seng holds its five-session gain of 4.03% while house prices keep falling, the market is paying for a floor under policy, not for a property recovery.

Playbook ✓: Own the China internet and consumption names on pullbacks, through KWEB and the Hong Kong listings, and keep property out of the book. Size for tariff news. The call changes if the next official manufacturing PMI prints below 50 or if the Hang Seng gives back its five-session gain of 4.03%. ⚠ Divergence: home prices are falling faster [45] while the equity market prices a recovery.

Macro Stance: The BOJ is moving toward hikes, but gradually. Goldman expects gradual hikes given the wage outlook [64], and major Japanese firms agreed to big wage increases, which keeps the policy debate live [65]. Growth is the drag. Japan downgraded fourth-quarter GDP and the outlook is clouded by US tariffs [66]. Japanese 10-year yields surged to near 16-year highs on rate-hike expectations in early March [67], and Pimco took profit on its Japan bond trade as rates rose [68].

Activity & Currency: The Nikkei 225 closed at 37,845.42, up 2.86% over five sessions but down 3.39% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). USD/JPY is at 149.3790, up 1.57% over five sessions and down 1.36% over 20, and the market is leaning on the 150 line. FOREX.com says USD/JPY hit a speed bump at 150 ahead of the BOJ and the FOMC [69]. Exports are holding up, partly because of stockpiling: Reuters reports that Japan’s February exports expanded on some stockpiling amid tariff fears [70]. Berkshire Hathaway lifted its stakes in five Japanese trading houses to almost 10% each [71].

Playbook ✓: Own the trading houses into a gradual BOJ path, since Berkshire’s stakes show who is willing to pay up for the corporate story, and hedge the yen on the exporters. The call changes if USD/JPY climbs back through 151.44, its level of 18 February, because a yen that weakens without a BOJ move would turn the exporter hedge into a trade on its own.

Macro Stance: Australia has absorbed more of the American slowdown than most markets. The ASX 200 closed at 7,860.40, down 7.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Macquarie warned of a bear market as US consumer spending collapses [72], and Morgan Stanley is bearish on the ASX, citing its correlation with Wall Street [73]. The RBA’s tone is more comfortable. It says the consumer rebound is here to stay [74], and that is the main counterweight in the data.

Demand & Financing: The structural problem is housing. New homes are set to fall 400,000 short of the national target [75], and an industry report puts half a million homes short of target [76]. Renters need a $130k income to afford the average property [77]. Power prices rise nearly 9% for some households from mid-year [78]. The financing channel is intact, for now. CBA says responsible lending rules shield it from rampant liar loans [79], and CBA and NAB chief executives are preparing for long-term Trump disruptions [80]. CBA’s share price is down 11.32% over 20 sessions, which says the market does not share that comfort (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). AUD/USD at 0.6382, up 1.63% over five sessions, helps the translation of local equities into dollars but adds little to domestic demand.

Playbook ✓: Stay underweight the big banks while CBA is 11.32% lower over 20 sessions, and avoid housing-linked names until shortage stories turn into approvals. Keep the miners at benchmark, since BHP, down only 3.30% over 20 sessions, is the part of the index holding up. The call changes if the ASX 200 reclaims the 8,481.00 level of 18 February, which would show the bear-market call is early.

Macro Stance: The NBP is on hold and says so. Yahoo Finance UK reports that the central bank chief sees no reason to cut Polish rates now [81], and TVN24 reports Glapiński calling the timing of disinflation ‘a rather distant horizon’ (‘Dość odległy horyzont’) [82]. The NBP’s March projection puts inflation at 4.9% this year and back at target only in 2027 [83]. A basket change flattered the February print: Money.pl reports that the change in inflation basket weights pulled it lower [84]. The labour market is the strength. Poland and the Czech Republic have the lowest unemployment in the EU [85]. The currency reflects it. Bankier reports that the dollar is at its cheapest in half a year and that the euro is below 4.20 zloty [86]. USD/PLN is at 3.8295, down 1.05% over five sessions and 3.38% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Warsaw and Kraków home prices fell year on year for the first time in three years, Strefa Inwestorów reports [87].

Markets: The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 53.21 PLN, up 8.41% over five sessions, and the Polish ETF EPOL is up 8.44% over the same stretch at 29.15 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). PKO BP rose 13.82% over five sessions to 80.04 PLN. The bank has crossed a milestone: Money.pl reports its market value passed 100 billion zloty for the first time [88], and Parkiet asks where the limit of gains lies [89]. The dividend is the support. Strefa Inwestorów says the 2025 dividend from PKO BP may be a record [90].

Fiscal & Politics: The budget is the weak spot. TVN24 reports that the state budget deficit keeps widening [91], and the finance minister has been clear on a cadastral property tax [92]. Fitch has issued its decision on Poland’s rating, Business Insider Polska reports [93], and that is the event the bond market is watching. Politics are tightening into the presidential vote. The Kyiv Independent says the Polish right is taking a hard line on Ukraine ahead of the vote [94], and Le Monde reports the far right picking up steam as the election approaches [95]. Bloomberg reports that Trump is straining ties with Poland [96]. A report finds Ukrainian immigrants have a ‘positive impact on Poland’s GDP and budget’ [97], and Forbes says Ukrainians in Poland pay far more in tax than they receive [98].

Corporate & Sectors: Orlen is the state anchor. Money.pl reports a loan from Orlen worth millions of dollars to Azoty [99], and a prosecutor closed its probe of a former Orlen chief executive [100]. Allegro sees rising 2025 earnings and proposes a $364 million buyback, Reuters says [101], and its shares are climbing on the buyback and results [102]. Dino is hiring 1,300 people [103] and its shares hit a record high [104]. Listed companies are earning from the military boom, Bankier reports [105]. Bank earnings are rising: Money.pl reports that PKO BP’s profit jumped by almost 4 billion zloty [106]. Consumers have filed more than 12.1 thousand lawsuits against banks to win back free loans, Rzeczpospolita reports [107].

Geopolitics & Security: Poland and the Baltic states plan to leave the anti-landmine convention, citing the Russian threat [108]. Tusk says Lithuanian evidence shows Russia was behind the fire that destroyed a Warsaw shopping centre [109]. Poland has asked NATO to raise the defence-spending minimum to 3% of GDP [110], and Estonia plans to lift its defence budget to 5% of GDP [111]. Donald Tusk announced military training for all men [112], and the president has urged Washington to move nuclear warheads to Polish territory [113]. Front-line NATO allies say landmines are now fair game in a warning to Russia [114].

New / Most Important: The signal that matters is that the rally is led by earnings and capital return, not by rate cuts. The NBP will not cut yet [81], PKO BP has passed a 100 billion zloty value [88], and the bank’s profit rose by almost 4 billion zloty [106]. Defence is the second leg: German parliament has passed the historic debt reform that paves the way for higher defence spending [115], which is a demand signal for the Polish defence names on the exchange.

Playbook ✓: Stay long the bank leaders, with PKO BP up 13.82% over five sessions, keep the defence names as a second leg, and do not fight a central bank that says it will not cut. Size the zloty trade for the NBP’s stance. ⚠ Divergence: the NBP projects inflation at 4.9% this year [83] while the dollar is at its cheapest in half a year against the zloty [86] and the WIG20 tracker is up 8.41% in five sessions.

Narrative: Technology is the AI consensus that broke. XLK closed at 212.15, down 12.39% over 20 sessions, and the drawdown is led by Apple and the software names (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Apple’s stock rout has taken nearly $700 billion off its market value since the record close [116], and the Wall Street Journal reports that Apple could stay in the penalty box on AI delays [117]. The driver that matters now is multiple compression rather than demand. Atlassian’s 30% fall in a month shows what happens when growth is not yet confirmed [118].

Reported: Adobe’s first-quarter beat did not save the stock, which fell 14% as concerns about AI growth overshadowed the results [119]. Workday’s full-year EPS missed expectations [120]. Broadcom’s March forecast had eased demand worries for AI chips [121], but Broadcom then fell on a report that Google may work with MediaTek on AI [122].

EPS Upside Watch: Micron is the cleanest set-up. Seeking Alpha calls the memory cycle prolonged [123], and the stock jumped 7% on three catalysts in mid-March [124]. Micron is up 14.23% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). An upside surprise would have to come from AI memory demand, not from the software names that just reset.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The consensus says AI capex is intact, and Nvidia’s keynote backs that case by unveiling Blackwell Ultra [125]. The signal against it is custom silicon. Google is reportedly preparing to partner with MediaTek on its next AI chip [126], and Broadcom fell on the report [122]. If Google’s chip work moves, the supply chain’s share shifts before the capex does.

Narrative: Communication services is split. XLC closed at 95.91, down 8.50% over 20 sessions, as the group prices a slowing ad market. Axios reports that ad growth is slowing [127], and Disney’s ‘Snow White’ opened after racist and sexist backlash [128]. The offset is subscription pricing power, where an analyst’s upgrade of Netflix cites future US price hikes [129]. XLC is down 1.40% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18).

Reported: Alphabet’s $32 billion Wiz deal is confirmed [130], which matters more for cloud security than for ad revenue. Mark Zuckerberg says Meta’s Llama models have hit one billion downloads [131], while Morningstar flags Meta’s new content-moderation policy as a risk to the stock [132].

EPS Upside Watch: Netflix is the set-up. Its shares rose on a bullish analyst upgrade citing potential future US price hikes and strong ad growth [129]. The stock is 10.22% lower over 20 sessions and 3.90% higher over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18), so the upgrade has room to work if pricing holds. The risk is that ad growth slows, which Axios says is already happening across the category [127].

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention says an ad slowdown hits the whole group. The Netflix upgrade says pricing power can outrun the ad cycle, so the weakness sits in advertising-exposed platforms rather than in subscription video.

Narrative: Financials mirror the sell-off. XLF closed at 49.03, down 6.02% over 20 sessions, and the big-bank group is trading the same growth scare as the index. Goldman Sachs is down 17.91% and Citigroup 17.03% over 20 sessions, while the regional-bank ETF KRE is down 11.62% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Bank of America’s survey shows investors pulling out of US equities at the biggest rate on record [1], a headwind for brokers and asset managers alike.

Reported: Affirm’s shares fell when Walmart switched its buy-now-pay-later partner to Klarna [133], and Affirm is down 46.04% over 20 sessions. Hong Kong’s AIA missed value-of-new-business estimates while unveiling a $1.6 billion buyback [134], a sign that insurers are returning capital as growth slows.

EPS Upside Watch: SoFi’s $5 billion personal-loan agreement with Blue Owl [135] is evidence that lending demand is still there, and Charles Schwab is up 7.02% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The set-up is a broker and lender that can grow loans through a slowdown. The watch item is credit commentary, not volume.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention is that higher-for-longer rates help banks. The bond market is doing the opposite: the 10-year is 26 bps lower over 20 observations, which narrows the net-interest margin story. Banks are being sold for the cycle, not for the rate.

Narrative: Energy is a geopolitical bid that has lost momentum. XLE closed at 91.34, flat over 20 sessions and up 4.53% over five, while WTI crude is at 66.90, down 6.89% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Reuters reports oil ticked up on the US attack on the Houthis [136], and Trump warned Iran of dire consequences for any further Houthi attacks [137]. Oil is near a two-week high on Mideast tensions [138].

Reported: US Energy Corp slid pre-market after a downbeat fourth quarter, with its CEO highlighting debt elimination [139]. Occidental is in the ‘4 reasons to love these prices’ camp [140], which is a bet on the price rather than on reported earnings.

EPS Upside Watch: Producers. The IEA’s March oil market report sets the supply picture [141], and OPEC is supporting a rise in production that could prove disastrous for prices [142], which caps the upside. Brent is down 6.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The set-up is a price-led beat if the Houthi premium holds, which is a bet on geopolitics rather than on demand.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention is that conflict lifts crude. Here crude fell 6.89% over 20 sessions even as US strikes on the Houthis escalated [143]. That suggests the market sees spare barrels and a demand problem, not a supply shock.

Narrative: Industrials are split between defence and tariffs. XLI closed at 131.88, down 4.87% over 20 sessions, while the aerospace and defence ETF ITA is down 1.30% and Lockheed Martin is up 9.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Tariffs on lumber and appliances raise the cost of new homes and remodels [144], while Reuters reports US homebuilding and manufacturing surged even as tariffs cast a pall over the recovery [145].

Reported: Graybar announced record 2024 financial results [146], and Steel Partners’ fourth-quarter earnings surged 94% year on year [147]. Daimler Truck is cutting costs in Europe by $1.1 billion after an earnings slump [148].

EPS Upside Watch: Defence suppliers are the upside. Europe’s rearmament is pulling demand toward its suppliers, and Airbus is leading a call for a sovereign fund and for buying European [149]. Lockheed is up 9.51% over 20 sessions, so the set-up is a defence beat rather than a housing-linked capital-goods beat.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention is that defence is a safe haven inside industrials. But QinetiQ’s shares tumbled on geopolitical uncertainty and contract delays [150]. Defence is not a single trade, and delays hit the names bought for the cycle.

Narrative: Consumer discretionary is the weakest group in the market. XLY closed at 193.50, down 14.52% over 20 sessions, and Tesla is down 36.37% in the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Retail sales came in weaker than expected [4], and consumer sentiment slumped in March to its lowest since 2022 [151]. Amazon’s Haul is struggling to keep up with Temu and Shein [152], and Target warned of a profit hit from the trade war [56].

Reported: Ulta issued weak guidance, citing consumer uncertainty and rising competition [153]. Hugo Boss warned of lingering uncertainty amid weak consumer sentiment [154]. Mercedes-Benz beat expectations on 2024 EPS [155], but the luxury read-across is poor.

EPS Upside Watch: Home Depot and Lowe’s are down 13.32% and 11.07% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Mortgage rates have fallen to a near three-month low [156], which sets up a remodel rebound, even though tariffs on appliances lift costs [144]. The upside surprise would come from volume, not pricing.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention says falling yields lift discretionary. The 10-year is 26 bps lower over 20 observations, yet XLY is down 14.52%. The consumer is the problem, not the discount rate, and sentiment at a since-2022 low [151] makes rate relief a weaker tailwind than usual.

Narrative: Staples are the defensive rotation. XLP closed at 79.75, down only 1.42% over 20 sessions against 14.52% for discretionary. PepsiCo’s agreement to acquire poppi for $1.95 billion [157] shows the sector is still buying growth while shoppers are squeezed, as Dollar General’s chief warned [158].

Reported: Alimentation Couche-Tard missed quarterly revenue estimates on lower fuel demand [159]. Dollar General warned that consumers are cash-strapped and that 2025 won’t be better [158], and it will close 141 stores [160].

EPS Upside Watch: Input costs are the set-up. Egg prices have dropped, though many shoppers have not noticed [161], which helps food margins. Costco is pressuring suppliers in mainland China to cut prices [162], a margin tailwind for the buyer and a squeeze for the supplier.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The convention says falling yields lift bond-proxy staples. Here the staples are holding without the rate tailwind: the 10-year is 26 bps lower over 20 observations, and the sector is still lower. The rotation is about earnings durability, not about rates.

The Motley Fool's question about whether D-Wave is still a buy [255] shows the buy case is being argued, not assumed. geo.label: hold / data dependent
parts: Macro Stance

Wall Street is in a correction rather than a crash, and the Fed meets into it. The S&P 500 closed at 5,614.66 on 18 March, down 8.40% over 20 sessions, while the Nasdaq 100 is 12.10% lower over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Reuters reported Bank of America’s survey showing the biggest drop in US equity allocation on record, which the bank calls a ‘bull crash’ [[n3808]]. Business Insider reports that investors have dumped a record amount of US stock as stagflation fears bite [[n3838]]. The growth data are softer than the inflation data. February payrolls rose by 151,000 [[n10269]], retail sales came in weaker than expected [[n10824]], and US CPI slid under consensus to 2.8% [[n10551]]. Strategists say the sell-off has ‘further to go’ as the Fed and tariff deadlines loom [[n3812]].
Rates & Curve

The curve is positively sloped. The 10-year closed at 4.29% and the 2-year at 4.04%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +25 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-18). Over 20 observations the move is bull flattening: the 2-year fell 25 bps and the 10-year fell 26 bps, so the spread narrowed by 1 bp. Over five observations the front end gave back a little ground, with the 2-year up 10 bps and the 10-year up 1 bp (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-18). The 3-month bill sits at 4.34%, keeping the 10Y−3M spread at −5 bps. The bond market is pricing a growth scare, not an inflation scare. The VIX rose 5.80% in the last session to 21.70 and is up 41.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The dollar index is at 103.24 index points, down 3.56% over 20 sessions, so the Treasury rally is not a dollar story.
New / Most Important

The decision that matters is the Fed’s on March 19. Bitcoin traders are already positioning around it, with one whale placing a $368 million short at 40x leverage ahead of the meeting [[n1821]]. Expectations had already moved toward easing, with Bloomberg reporting that the Fed is expected to cut twice this year, starting in September [[n11158]]. Options are underpricing the reaction, according to Nasdaq’s volatility note [[n11297]]. Powell is contending with what the Wall Street Journal calls a double threat of economic chaos and political hostility [[n11390]], and Trump’s nomination of Governor Michelle Bowman as vice chair for supervision adds a governance question to the meeting [[n11331]].
Playbook ✓

Own duration rather than the index. The 10-year at 4.29% has room to rally if the Fed sounds patient, and TLT at 90.71 USD is already up 2.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Trim the AI leaders into strength: the Nasdaq 100 is down 12.10% over 20 sessions and XLK is down 12.39% in the same window. Keep a hedge, because a VIX at 21.70 does not pay for complacency. The call changes if the 10-year climbs back above 4.55%, the level it held 20 observations ago, since a bond rally that fails would leave duration without protection. Rotate rather than exit: staples and utilities have held up better than discretionary, which is down 14.52% over 20 sessions.

geo.label: fiscal turn / easing bias
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is turning from restraint to spending, and the market is rewarding it. On 18 March the German parliament passed the debt-rule reform and a half-trillion-euro fund [[n3425]]. Bankier reports that the Bundestag changed the constitution and left the military budget without limits [[n5951]]. BBC reports that Germany voted for a historic boost to defence and infrastructure spending [[n3428]]. The Euro Stoxx 50 closed at 5,485.01, up 3.30% over five sessions, and the DAX is up 4.71% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). BNP Paribas says euro strength, not dollar weakness, is driving markets [[n3419]]. The ECB has already eased, cutting its key rate to 2.5% on 6 March [[n3174]], and the Bundesbank is using AI to prove the ECB’s dovish bias [[n3413]].
Credit & Inflation

Credit is quiet, but the cost of borrowing matters. France’s borrowing costs were near a 14-year high before the Fitch review [[n3279]], and Moody’s cut Romania’s outlook on budget risks [[n3331]]. The fiscal impulse runs the other way. DIW says Germany’s expansion would boost GDP from 2026 [[n3324]], and German investor morale rose sharply in March [[n3424]]. Inflation is the constraint on the ECB. Lagarde warned that trade and defence shocks risk amplifying euro-zone inflation [[n3255]], while the fall in German inflation gives the ECB more room to ease [[n3322]]. The OECD says Trump’s trade wars are slowing global growth and fuelling inflation [[n3402]].
New / Most Important

The signal that matters is that the German fiscal shift has passed parliament, not just a proposal [[n3425]]. Reuters has broken down the agreed plan [[n3440]], and DW puts the impact at €1 trillion [[n3410]]. Defence is the direct beneficiary. Rheinmetall is up 55.63% over 20 sessions and 25.26% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18), and Reuters reported it overtook Volkswagen’s market value on 13 March [[n6166]]. Reuters also reports that Europe’s top money managers are only starting to bring defence stocks in from the cold [[n3275]]. Everyone loves German rearmament, Bloomberg wrote on 17 March [[n3377]].
Playbook ✓

Own the German fiscal chain on dips, meaning industrials, infrastructure and defence, but size it for a ceasefire. Avoid the autos: the European auto ETF is down 5.10% over 20 sessions, and BMW’s annual net profit fell 37% (CNBC, 14 March) [[n2795]]. Euro strength argues for hedging dollar-earning exporters rather than the German domestic names. The call changes if Russia–Ukraine talks produce a truce that removes the defence premium [[n4458]], or if the budget fails to show up in German orders.

geo.label: policy push / property drag
parts: Macro Stance

Beijing is spending its political capital on consumption. CNBC reports the plan to ‘vigorously boost consumption’ as a bid to shore up the economy [[n1323]], SCMP counts a 30-point toolbox [[n1328]], and calls the package the most comprehensive since the 1970s [[n1371]]. Equities are responding. The Hang Seng closed at 24,740.57, up 7.68% over 20 sessions and 2.46% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The question is whether the activity data confirm the plan, and so far they only partly do. Beijing’s consumption push is also a labour story: lawmakers are targeting the job-market bias against over-35s [[n1211]].
PMIs & Activity

February’s non-manufacturing PMI was 50.4 [[n0761]]. Industrial output rose 5.9% in January and February, beating expectations [[n1370]], and retail sales were up 4% over the first two months [[n1436]]. The growth is policy-led, not private-demand-led. Reuters says retail sales are picking up as Beijing turns to consumers to ease US trade pressure [[n1363]]. Prices are the caution: consumer prices fell in February and remain flat in a sluggish economy [[n0990]]. What would confirm the view is the next official manufacturing PMI not falling, with retail sales holding up once the trade-in subsidies are working through the data.
Credit Impulse

Credit is a policy story for now. The central bank says it will create ‘more tools’ to shore up the economy [[n1263]], and Bank of China is setting up a $7 billion fund to support technology development [[n1253]]. Foreign investors are lining up for high-yielding Chinese bank debt [[n1383]]. The test is whether the tools reach households and private borrowers, rather than state banks and technology funds. Developers still need the banks: ICBC (Asia) is backing Hong Kong developers with loan support as the sector struggles [[n1396]].
Property

Property is the drag the equity rally does not price. Bloomberg reports that home prices are falling at a faster pace despite revival efforts [[n1322]], and Reuters says the slump persists as stimulus struggles to stabilise the sector [[n1332]]. Developers diverge. Sunac warns of a wider loss for 2024 [[n1414]], while Country Garden’s unit forecasts higher annual earnings [[n1285]]. China Vanke’s Hong Kong unit reports strong flat sales despite mortgage concerns [[n1303]]. Foreign funds have been selling China’s commercial properties for a fourth year, SCMP reports [[n6123]].
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Fiscal and trade policy pull in opposite directions. Beijing is doubling down on trade-ins to boost sluggish consumption [[n1392]], but the OECD finds that Trump’s tariffs will slow China’s economy and impede global trade [[n1514]]. Importers are rushing to beat the tariffs and living on the edge [[n1475]]. Trump says Xi may visit the US in the not-too-distant future [[n1366]], though analysts doubt a summit will make headway on trade [[n1524]]. Target, which relies on China for 30% of its merchandise, warned of a profit hit as the trade war bites [[n1415]]. Chinese economists are calling for a wider social safety net to nurture consumption [[n1469]].
Markets & Flows

Equities are leading the data. The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,429.76 index points, up 3.17% over 20 sessions, and ASHR, the CSI 300 ETF, is at 27.60 USD, up 3.10% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). KWEB, the internet ETF, is up 6.17% over 20 sessions at 37.83 USD. USD/CNY at 7.2327 is 0.28% lower over 20 sessions, so the yuan is firming, not sliding. Reuters argues that Chinese stocks offer a hedge against fading US exceptionalism [[n1457]], and Business Insider explains why China’s stock market is roaring after investors fled in 2024 [[n1317]]. Hong Kong’s stock market is booming while Wall Street is in turmoil, Bloomberg reports [[n1203]], and China’s stock rerating is widening the premiums in the ADRs of Alibaba and Li Auto [[n1185]]. The tech leg is AI. Alibaba has revamped its Quark search engine into an AI super assistant [[n1165]], and Tencent is pushing open-source 3D generation tools [[n1505]].
New / Most Important

The new signal is the scale of the consumption push, paired with an equity market that is trading the policy rather than the property data. The plan to ‘vigorously boost consumption’ is an explicit bid to shore up growth [[n1323]], and the package is the most comprehensive in decades [[n1371]]. Tariffs are the offset. If the Hang Seng holds its five-session gain of 4.03% while house prices keep falling, the market is paying for a floor under policy, not for a property recovery.
Playbook ✓

Own the China internet and consumption names on pullbacks, through KWEB and the Hong Kong listings, and keep property out of the book. Size for tariff news. The call changes if the next official manufacturing PMI prints below 50 or if the Hang Seng gives back its five-session gain of 4.03%. ⚠ Divergence: home prices are falling faster [[n1322]] while the equity market prices a recovery.

geo.label: gradual hikes / weak yen
parts: Macro Stance

The BOJ is moving toward hikes, but gradually. Goldman expects gradual hikes given the wage outlook [[n5273]], and major Japanese firms agreed to big wage increases, which keeps the policy debate live [[n5149]]. Growth is the drag. Japan downgraded fourth-quarter GDP and the outlook is clouded by US tariffs [[n5095]]. Japanese 10-year yields surged to near 16-year highs on rate-hike expectations in early March [[n5057]], and Pimco took profit on its Japan bond trade as rates rose [[n5221]].
Activity & Currency

The Nikkei 225 closed at 37,845.42, up 2.86% over five sessions but down 3.39% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). USD/JPY is at 149.3790, up 1.57% over five sessions and down 1.36% over 20, and the market is leaning on the 150 line. FOREX.com says USD/JPY hit a speed bump at 150 ahead of the BOJ and the FOMC [[n0529]]. Exports are holding up, partly because of stockpiling: Reuters reports that Japan’s February exports expanded on some stockpiling amid tariff fears [[n5275]]. Berkshire Hathaway lifted its stakes in five Japanese trading houses to almost 10% each [[n8329]].
Playbook ✓

Own the trading houses into a gradual BOJ path, since Berkshire’s stakes show who is willing to pay up for the corporate story, and hedge the yen on the exporters. The call changes if USD/JPY climbs back through 151.44, its level of 18 February, because a yen that weakens without a BOJ move would turn the exporter hedge into a trade on its own.

geo.label: housing shortfall / bear-market risk
parts: Macro Stance

Australia has absorbed more of the American slowdown than most markets. The ASX 200 closed at 7,860.40, down 7.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Macquarie warned of a bear market as US consumer spending collapses [[n0356]], and Morgan Stanley is bearish on the ASX, citing its correlation with Wall Street [[n0314]]. The RBA’s tone is more comfortable. It says the consumer rebound is here to stay [[n0439]], and that is the main counterweight in the data.
Demand & Financing

The structural problem is housing. New homes are set to fall 400,000 short of the national target [[n0456]], and an industry report puts half a million homes short of target [[n0447]]. Renters need a $130k income to afford the average property [[n0472]]. Power prices rise nearly 9% for some households from mid-year [[n0266]]. The financing channel is intact, for now. CBA says responsible lending rules shield it from rampant liar loans [[n0435]], and CBA and NAB chief executives are preparing for long-term Trump disruptions [[n0436]]. CBA’s share price is down 11.32% over 20 sessions, which says the market does not share that comfort (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). AUD/USD at 0.6382, up 1.63% over five sessions, helps the translation of local equities into dollars but adds little to domestic demand.
Playbook ✓

Stay underweight the big banks while CBA is 11.32% lower over 20 sessions, and avoid housing-linked names until shortage stories turn into approvals. Keep the miners at benchmark, since BHP, down only 3.30% over 20 sessions, is the part of the index holding up. The call changes if the ASX 200 reclaims the 8,481.00 level of 18 February, which would show the bear-market call is early.

geo.label: bank-led rally / rates on hold
parts: Macro Stance

The NBP is on hold and says so. Yahoo Finance UK reports that the central bank chief sees no reason to cut Polish rates now [[n3291]], and TVN24 reports Glapiński calling the timing of disinflation ‘a rather distant horizon’ (‘Dość odległy horyzont’) [[n5776]]. The NBP’s March projection puts inflation at 4.9% this year and back at target only in 2027 [[n5832]]. A basket change flattered the February print: Money.pl reports that the change in inflation basket weights pulled it lower [[n5828]]. The labour market is the strength. Poland and the Czech Republic have the lowest unemployment in the EU [[n5620]]. The currency reflects it. Bankier reports that the dollar is at its cheapest in half a year and that the euro is below 4.20 zloty [[n5953]]. USD/PLN is at 3.8295, down 1.05% over five sessions and 3.38% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Warsaw and Kraków home prices fell year on year for the first time in three years, Strefa Inwestorów reports [[n5681]].
Markets

The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 53.21 PLN, up 8.41% over five sessions, and the Polish ETF EPOL is up 8.44% over the same stretch at 29.15 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). PKO BP rose 13.82% over five sessions to 80.04 PLN. The bank has crossed a milestone: Money.pl reports its market value passed 100 billion zloty for the first time [[n5961]], and Parkiet asks where the limit of gains lies [[n5972]]. The dividend is the support. Strefa Inwestorów says the 2025 dividend from PKO BP may be a record [[n5775]].
Fiscal & Politics

The budget is the weak spot. TVN24 reports that the state budget deficit keeps widening [[n5890]], and the finance minister has been clear on a cadastral property tax [[n5915]]. Fitch has issued its decision on Poland’s rating, Business Insider Polska reports [[n5854]], and that is the event the bond market is watching. Politics are tightening into the presidential vote. The Kyiv Independent says the Polish right is taking a hard line on Ukraine ahead of the vote [[n5441]], and Le Monde reports the far right picking up steam as the election approaches [[n5396]]. Bloomberg reports that Trump is straining ties with Poland [[n5391]]. A report finds Ukrainian immigrants have a ‘positive impact on Poland’s GDP and budget’ [[n5397]], and Forbes says Ukrainians in Poland pay far more in tax than they receive [[n5394]].
Corporate & Sectors

Orlen is the state anchor. Money.pl reports a loan from Orlen worth millions of dollars to Azoty [[n5987]], and a prosecutor closed its probe of a former Orlen chief executive [[n5991]]. Allegro sees rising 2025 earnings and proposes a $364 million buyback, Reuters says [[n5370]], and its shares are climbing on the buyback and results [[n5788]]. Dino is hiring 1,300 people [[n5772]] and its shares hit a record high [[n5651]]. Listed companies are earning from the military boom, Bankier reports [[n5655]]. Bank earnings are rising: Money.pl reports that PKO BP’s profit jumped by almost 4 billion zloty [[n5787]]. Consumers have filed more than 12.1 thousand lawsuits against banks to win back free loans, Rzeczpospolita reports [[n5970]].
Geopolitics & Security

Poland and the Baltic states plan to leave the anti-landmine convention, citing the Russian threat [[n5435]]. Tusk says Lithuanian evidence shows Russia was behind the fire that destroyed a Warsaw shopping centre [[n5416]]. Poland has asked NATO to raise the defence-spending minimum to 3% of GDP [[n5334]], and Estonia plans to lift its defence budget to 5% of GDP [[n5422]]. Donald Tusk announced military training for all men [[n5333]], and the president has urged Washington to move nuclear warheads to Polish territory [[n5378]]. Front-line NATO allies say landmines are now fair game in a warning to Russia [[n5423]].
New / Most Important

The signal that matters is that the rally is led by earnings and capital return, not by rate cuts. The NBP will not cut yet [[n3291]], PKO BP has passed a 100 billion zloty value [[n5961]], and the bank’s profit rose by almost 4 billion zloty [[n5787]]. Defence is the second leg: German parliament has passed the historic debt reform that paves the way for higher defence spending [[n3426]], which is a demand signal for the Polish defence names on the exchange.
Playbook ✓

Stay long the bank leaders, with PKO BP up 13.82% over five sessions, keep the defence names as a second leg, and do not fight a central bank that says it will not cut. Size the zloty trade for the NBP’s stance. ⚠ Divergence: the NBP projects inflation at 4.9% this year [[n5832]] while the dollar is at its cheapest in half a year against the zloty [[n5953]] and the WIG20 tracker is up 8.41% in five sessions.
Narrative

Technology is the AI consensus that broke. XLK closed at 212.15, down 12.39% over 20 sessions, and the drawdown is led by Apple and the software names (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Apple’s stock rout has taken nearly $700 billion off its market value since the record close [[n8833]], and the Wall Street Journal reports that Apple could stay in the penalty box on AI delays [[n8825]]. The driver that matters now is multiple compression rather than demand. Atlassian’s 30% fall in a month shows what happens when growth is not yet confirmed [[n8300]].
Reported

Adobe’s first-quarter beat did not save the stock, which fell 14% as concerns about AI growth overshadowed the results [[n2682]]. Workday’s full-year EPS missed expectations [[n2781]]. Broadcom’s March forecast had eased demand worries for AI chips [[n2121]], but Broadcom then fell on a report that Google may work with MediaTek on AI [[n8326]].
EPS Upside Watch

Micron is the cleanest set-up. Seeking Alpha calls the memory cycle prolonged [[n2508]], and the stock jumped 7% on three catalysts in mid-March [[n2741]]. Micron is up 14.23% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). An upside surprise would have to come from AI memory demand, not from the software names that just reset.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The consensus says AI capex is intact, and Nvidia’s keynote backs that case by unveiling Blackwell Ultra [[n3001]]. The signal against it is custom silicon. Google is reportedly preparing to partner with MediaTek on its next AI chip [[n4509]], and Broadcom fell on the report [[n8326]]. If Google’s chip work moves, the supply chain’s share shifts before the capex does.
Narrative

Communication services is split. XLC closed at 95.91, down 8.50% over 20 sessions, as the group prices a slowing ad market. Axios reports that ad growth is slowing [[n8813]], and Disney’s ‘Snow White’ opened after racist and sexist backlash [[n8897]]. The offset is subscription pricing power, where an analyst’s upgrade of Netflix cites future US price hikes [[n2912]]. XLC is down 1.40% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18).
Reported

Alphabet’s $32 billion Wiz deal is confirmed [[n2976]], which matters more for cloud security than for ad revenue. Mark Zuckerberg says Meta’s Llama models have hit one billion downloads [[n2995]], while Morningstar flags Meta’s new content-moderation policy as a risk to the stock [[n3019]].
EPS Upside Watch

Netflix is the set-up. Its shares rose on a bullish analyst upgrade citing potential future US price hikes and strong ad growth [[n2912]]. The stock is 10.22% lower over 20 sessions and 3.90% higher over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18), so the upgrade has room to work if pricing holds. The risk is that ad growth slows, which Axios says is already happening across the category [[n8813]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says an ad slowdown hits the whole group. The Netflix upgrade says pricing power can outrun the ad cycle, so the weakness sits in advertising-exposed platforms rather than in subscription video.
Narrative

Financials mirror the sell-off. XLF closed at 49.03, down 6.02% over 20 sessions, and the big-bank group is trading the same growth scare as the index. Goldman Sachs is down 17.91% and Citigroup 17.03% over 20 sessions, while the regional-bank ETF KRE is down 11.62% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Bank of America’s survey shows investors pulling out of US equities at the biggest rate on record [[n3808]], a headwind for brokers and asset managers alike.
Reported

Affirm’s shares fell when Walmart switched its buy-now-pay-later partner to Klarna [[n8250]], and Affirm is down 46.04% over 20 sessions. Hong Kong’s AIA missed value-of-new-business estimates while unveiling a $1.6 billion buyback [[n1202]], a sign that insurers are returning capital as growth slows.
EPS Upside Watch

SoFi’s $5 billion personal-loan agreement with Blue Owl [[n6178]] is evidence that lending demand is still there, and Charles Schwab is up 7.02% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The set-up is a broker and lender that can grow loans through a slowdown. The watch item is credit commentary, not volume.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that higher-for-longer rates help banks. The bond market is doing the opposite: the 10-year is 26 bps lower over 20 observations, which narrows the net-interest margin story. Banks are being sold for the cycle, not for the rate.
Narrative

Energy is a geopolitical bid that has lost momentum. XLE closed at 91.34, flat over 20 sessions and up 4.53% over five, while WTI crude is at 66.90, down 6.89% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Reuters reports oil ticked up on the US attack on the Houthis [[n1410]], and Trump warned Iran of dire consequences for any further Houthi attacks [[n4812]]. Oil is near a two-week high on Mideast tensions [[n0527]].
Reported

US Energy Corp slid pre-market after a downbeat fourth quarter, with its CEO highlighting debt elimination [[n6191]]. Occidental is in the ‘4 reasons to love these prices’ camp [[n2920]], which is a bet on the price rather than on reported earnings.
EPS Upside Watch

Producers. The IEA’s March oil market report sets the supply picture [[n7523]], and OPEC is supporting a rise in production that could prove disastrous for prices [[n8759]], which caps the upside. Brent is down 6.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The set-up is a price-led beat if the Houthi premium holds, which is a bet on geopolitics rather than on demand.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that conflict lifts crude. Here crude fell 6.89% over 20 sessions even as US strikes on the Houthis escalated [[n4461]]. That suggests the market sees spare barrels and a demand problem, not a supply shock.
Narrative

Industrials are split between defence and tariffs. XLI closed at 131.88, down 4.87% over 20 sessions, while the aerospace and defence ETF ITA is down 1.30% and Lockheed Martin is up 9.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Tariffs on lumber and appliances raise the cost of new homes and remodels [[n10830]], while Reuters reports US homebuilding and manufacturing surged even as tariffs cast a pall over the recovery [[n9187]].
Reported

Graybar announced record 2024 financial results [[n2728]], and Steel Partners’ fourth-quarter earnings surged 94% year on year [[n3008]]. Daimler Truck is cutting costs in Europe by $1.1 billion after an earnings slump [[n2804]].
EPS Upside Watch

Defence suppliers are the upside. Europe’s rearmament is pulling demand toward its suppliers, and Airbus is leading a call for a sovereign fund and for buying European [[n8216]]. Lockheed is up 9.51% over 20 sessions, so the set-up is a defence beat rather than a housing-linked capital-goods beat.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that defence is a safe haven inside industrials. But QinetiQ’s shares tumbled on geopolitical uncertainty and contract delays [[n2929]]. Defence is not a single trade, and delays hit the names bought for the cycle.
Narrative

Consumer discretionary is the weakest group in the market. XLY closed at 193.50, down 14.52% over 20 sessions, and Tesla is down 36.37% in the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Retail sales came in weaker than expected [[n10824]], and consumer sentiment slumped in March to its lowest since 2022 [[n10697]]. Amazon’s Haul is struggling to keep up with Temu and Shein [[n8275]], and Target warned of a profit hit from the trade war [[n1415]].
Reported

Ulta issued weak guidance, citing consumer uncertainty and rising competition [[n2772]]. Hugo Boss warned of lingering uncertainty amid weak consumer sentiment [[n10618]]. Mercedes-Benz beat expectations on 2024 EPS [[n2739]], but the luxury read-across is poor.
EPS Upside Watch

Home Depot and Lowe’s are down 13.32% and 11.07% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Mortgage rates have fallen to a near three-month low [[n10638]], which sets up a remodel rebound, even though tariffs on appliances lift costs [[n10830]]. The upside surprise would come from volume, not pricing.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says falling yields lift discretionary. The 10-year is 26 bps lower over 20 observations, yet XLY is down 14.52%. The consumer is the problem, not the discount rate, and sentiment at a since-2022 low [[n10697]] makes rate relief a weaker tailwind than usual.
Narrative

Staples are the defensive rotation. XLP closed at 79.75, down only 1.42% over 20 sessions against 14.52% for discretionary. PepsiCo’s agreement to acquire poppi for $1.95 billion [[n10821]] shows the sector is still buying growth while shoppers are squeezed, as Dollar General’s chief warned [[n3556]].
Reported

Alimentation Couche-Tard missed quarterly revenue estimates on lower fuel demand [[n2965]]. Dollar General warned that consumers are cash-strapped and that 2025 won’t be better [[n3556]], and it will close 141 stores [[n3646]].
EPS Upside Watch

Input costs are the set-up. Egg prices have dropped, though many shoppers have not noticed [[n10868]], which helps food margins. Costco is pressuring suppliers in mainland China to cut prices [[n1470]], a margin tailwind for the buyer and a squeeze for the supplier.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says falling yields lift bond-proxy staples. Here the staples are holding without the rate tailwind: the 10-year is 26 bps lower over 20 observations, and the sector is still lower. The rotation is about earnings durability, not about rates.
Narrative

Health care is the defensive pocket with a policy overhang. XLV closed at 146.84, up 1.61% over 20 sessions, while the obesity-drug trade is under pressure. Hims & Hers tumbled after the FDA warned about unapproved weight-loss drugs [[n6425]], and Novo Nordisk slid 4% on Roche’s $5.3 billion obesity deal [[n6977]].
Reported

Sangamo Therapeutics slid after hours on a fourth-quarter miss, though retail traders kept the faith [[n6397]]. Merck is planning 163 layoffs as it prepares to shutter a Pennsylvania manufacturing site [[n10812]].
EPS Upside Watch

Vertex is on Evercore’s all-weather list [[n7833]], and Citi argues small and mid-cap biotechs are the alternative to large caps [[n7322]]. The upside is a rebound in smaller biotech from a base where private-equity and venture money to biotech is at its lowest since 2019 [[n0637]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention says FDA enforcement is a small-cap risk. Here it reached Hims, a large retail favourite [[n6425]], and an FDA ruling could end affordable access to weight-loss drugs [[n7401]]. For the obesity names, policy is the binding variable, not earnings.
Narrative

Materials are a tariff-and-gold story. XLB closed at 86.91, down 4.48% over 20 sessions. Gold hit a record high of over $3,000 on geopolitical tensions [[n8959]], and Luxembourg’s gold reserves top €200 million amid the global rally [[n9038]]. Borouge proposed a share buyback after its stock slid on merger news [[n3730]]. Cornerstone announced the sale of its sulfuric acid operations to Ecovyst [[n8878]].
EPS Upside Watch

Gold producers have the cleanest upside. With gold at record levels, miners’ revenue leverage is high: GDX is up 7.97% over 20 sessions and SLV is up 3.14%, while copper, a grid and data-centre metal, is up 8.90% over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The surprise will come from price, not volume.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Consensus treats gold as the fear trade. Gold is rising while the S&P falls, but the dollar index is down 3.56% over 20 sessions, so the metal’s bid is about the dollar and real rates rather than a global growth scare.
Narrative

Real estate is a rates trade with a tariff tax. XLRE closed at 41.92, down 0.69% over 20 sessions, while the 10-year fell 26 bps over the same window (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-18). Mortgage rates have plunged to near a three-month low [[n10638]], but tariffs on lumber and appliances raise the cost of new homes and remodels [[n10830]]. New construction momentum is stalling as costs rise [[n10897]].
Reported
Bridgemarq’s full-year 2024 earnings beat expectations [[n2843]], and Prologis is described as a best-in-class income-growth REIT [[n2864]].
EPS Upside Watch

Housing-linked service firms. Mortgage demand turns as rates fall, and the Rocket–Redfin deal could make home buying more convenient, and more expensive [[n10654]]. The set-up is volume, if rates hold near these levels.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that lower yields lift REITs. XLRE is still lower over 20 sessions despite the 26 bp fall in the 10-year. Rate relief is being offset by build costs, while Politico argues Trump is providing an unexpected boost to the housing market [[n10880]], and that is the divergence to watch.
Narrative

Utilities are the power-demand trade, and nuclear is its loudest voice. XLU closed at 78.65, down 1.49% over 20 sessions but up 1.60% over five. Amazon, Google and Meta support tripling nuclear power by 2050 [[n6016]], and Constellation is a nuclear leader as demand hits early stages [[n6207]]. Forbes says solar-plus-storage is the fastest, cheapest way to meet surging power demand [[n9139]].
Reported

Southern Company is among the best electric utility stocks to buy now, according to Yahoo Finance [[n2941]]. NextEra cut XPLR Infrastructure loose [[n2848]], which is a capital-structure story rather than an operating one.
EPS Upside Watch

Power prices. Some Australian households face rises of nearly 9% from mid-year [[n0266]], an analogue of the pricing power utilities can earn. In the US the set-up runs through rate cases: Xcel says its proposed gas and energy prices may add more than $2.50 to Colorado residential bills [[n2855]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that utilities are bond proxies. This group is rising on power demand, not on yields, and the 10-year’s 26 bp fall has not lifted it. Nuclear names are the sentiment test: NuScale and Oklo surged as Amazon and Google bet on nuclear, but retail sentiment pulled back [[n6060]].
Narrative

European autos are the weakest link in the European rally. The iShares auto ETF closed at 52.65 EUR, down 5.10% over 20 sessions, while the STOXX 600 is only 0.52% lower over the same window (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Audi will cut 7,500 jobs by 2029 amid Chinese competition and an EV slowdown [[n8953]], and its profits are tanking on weak demand and Chinese price wars [[n2970]].
Reported

BMW’s annual net profit fell 37% and it warned of subdued Chinese demand [[n2795]], and BMW expects a €1 billion hit to earnings from escalating tariffs [[n2792]]. Daimler Truck is cutting costs in Europe after its earnings slump [[n2804]].
EPS Upside Watch

Mercedes-Benz beat expectations on 2024 EPS [[n2739]], and BMW expects US tariffs to be temporary [[n2793]]. If tariffs prove temporary, the autos are set up for a relief rally, and the April 2 tariff deadline that Stellantis is preparing for is the test [[n9154]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that Chinese price wars hurt only the Chinese brands. Volkswagen is bringing forward its first software-defined vehicle with Rivian’s help [[n3013]], which suggests the European majors are finding ways to compete on cost and time, not only on volume.
Narrative

Semiconductors are split between Nvidia’s AI demand and a fight over memory and foundry share. SOXX closed at 201.47, down 11.15% over 20 sessions. Nvidia unveiled Blackwell Ultra at its keynote [[n3001]], and OpenAI’s first Stargate site will hold up to 400,000 Nvidia chips [[n9101]]. The foundry map is the pricing lever: tariff threats are spurring TSMC’s Taiwan peers to seek US expansion [[n4799]].
Reported

Samsung’s CEO says the company will pursue deals as it struggles for growth [[n9131]]. Foxconn forecast strong first-quarter revenue after a profit miss [[n2809]]. Broadcom’s 77% AI revenue spike [[n2243]] is the latest print for the custom-silicon names.
EPS Upside Watch

Micron and Broadcom are the memory and custom-silicon names. Micron is up 14.23% over five sessions, and the memory cycle is described as prolonged [[n2508]]. A forecast beat is the set-up if Stargate-scale orders convert into revenue.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that Nvidia drives the group. The signal against it is the foundry pitch: TSMC proposed a foundry joint venture to Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom [[n6662]], which redraws the foundry map. Intel, up 31.04% over five sessions after its CEO appointment [[n6146]], is the stock most exposed to that redraw.

earnings_pattern.title: Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
parts: Rewarded

DocuSign shares surged 14% on strong earnings and an AI boost [[n2829]]. Xiaomi’s shares were pricing near-perfect execution after a 300% rally [[n2839]], so the outlook, not the beat, was the bar to clear. Steel Partners’ fourth-quarter earnings surged 94% year on year, with revenue climbing 6.6% [[n3008]].
Punished

Adobe shares fell 14% even after a better-than-expected quarter [[n2682]], because the guidance overshadowed the beat [[n2680]]. Adobe is down 9.75% over five sessions and 15.67% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). ContextLogic slipped after hours on a fourth-quarter miss [[n2700]], and Ulta issued weak guidance, citing consumer uncertainty and rising competition [[n2772]]. BMW’s annual net profit fell 37%, with a warning on subdued Chinese demand [[n2795]].
Pattern

The market pays for guidance and punishes the gap between a beat and the outlook. Rewarded names raised or held their outlooks. Punished names beat and then guided lower, or missed outright. The rule works in the other direction too: Broadcom’s solid forecast eased demand worries for AI chips [[n2121]], and that is what lifted the AI-hardware names that held up. DocuSign’s 14% jump [[n2829]] and Adobe’s 14% fall [[n2682]] came one day apart, which says the market is grading the outlook, not the quarter.
Attention into EPS

The set-up for the next prints is about guidance. Nvidia’s keynote has passed, and the stock is still 17.20% lower over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18), so the market will test whether Blackwell Ultra demand shows up in outlooks [[n3001]]. Netflix’s upgrade cites pricing power and ad growth [[n2912]], which puts its next outlook under the microscope. The EPS risk sits in names where the beat is already in the price, such as Adobe after its 14% reaction.
Playbook

Own the guidance raisers and avoid beat-and-guide-lower names until their outlooks stabilise. Adobe is the template for a sell-the-beat set-up, and Netflix is the template for a pricing-power upgrade. The call changes if a beat is paired with a raised outlook at the next print, because then the rule flips and the sell-off becomes an entry.

underowned.title: China equities — the unloved rally on policy
parts: Attention Gap

Foreign money left Chinese equities through 2024, and it is only now returning. Business Insider explains why China’s stock market is roaring after investors fled in 2024 [[n1317]], and Reuters says Donald Trump has made Chinese stocks, somewhat, great again [[n1270]]. Inflows into Chinese stocks were large in February, according to the Institute of International Finance [[n1188]]. A Reuters commentary calls Chinese stocks a hedge against fading US exceptionalism [[n1457]]. The gap is between the rally and the flows: the rally is recent, and February’s inflows are the first hard evidence of money coming back.
Exposure & Risk

FXI is at 38.49 USD, up 9.04% over 20 sessions, KWEB is at 37.83 USD, up 6.17%, and ASHR is at 27.60 USD, up 3.10% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The risk is that the Hang Seng’s 20-session gain of 7.68% rests on policy rather than on earnings. Tariffs remain the overhang, and the OECD expects Trump’s tariffs to slow China’s economy [[n1514]].
Trigger to Watch

The next official manufacturing PMI, and the first sign that the consumption plan reaches household spending [[n1371]]. A Trump–Xi summit is undated, and analysts doubt it will deliver trade progress [[n1524]].

underowned.title: Japan equities — Buffett’s trading-house stakes
parts: Attention Gap

Berkshire lifted its stakes in five Japanese trading houses to almost 10% each [[n8329]], and Warren Buffett is investing more money in Japan amid the US selloff [[n11338]]. The Nikkei is 3.39% lower over 20 sessions, so the interest is not showing up in the index yet. Reuters reports that Hong Kong hedge fund Polymer Capital is joining a rush to debut pure Japan funds [[n3844]], which means institutional interest is only starting to build.
Exposure & Risk

EWJ is at 70.89 USD, up 1.13% over 20 sessions and 3.85% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Toyota is up 2.36% over 20 sessions, while Tokyo Electron is down 9.92%, so the exposure is to the chip cycle as much as to the trading houses. The yen is the currency risk, with USD/JPY at 149.3790.
Trigger to Watch
A BOJ decision that confirms gradual hikes [[n5273]], which would support the trading houses, and a sharp yen rally that hits exporters. Either one turns the trade into consensus or breaks it.

underowned.title: European defence — the funds arriving late
parts: Attention Gap

European money managers are only now starting to bring defence stocks in from the cold [[n3275]]. Rheinmetall’s market value overtook Volkswagen’s [[n6166]], and Investing.com called the European defence move parabolic as war spending surged [[n6036]]. Rheinmetall is at 1,445.50 EUR, up 55.63% over 20 sessions and 25.26% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Siemens is up 4.77% over 20 sessions. The risk is a ceasefire: Trump and Putin are expected to speak as the US pushes for a Russia–Ukraine ceasefire [[n4458]], and a truce would remove part of the defence premium.
Trigger to Watch

Germany’s budget change has now passed [[n3425]]. The next test is the EU’s temporary exemption for defence spending, which EU ministers backed in principle [[n3220]]. Consensus arrives when those rules are in place and orders follow.

underowned.title: Small and mid-cap biotech — the cheap alternative to large caps
parts: Attention Gap

Citi argues small and mid-cap biotechs are the alternative to large caps [[n7322]], while private-equity and venture-capital flows to biotech are at their lowest since 2019 [[n0637]]. The biotech ETF XBI is at 86.17 USD, down 5.65% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18), so the group looks cheap without being loved.

XBI is the instrument, but single names carry FDA risk. Hims & Hers fell after the FDA’s warning on unapproved weight-loss drugs [[n6425]]. Layoffs are spreading through the sector: Pyxis is cutting 20% of its staff [[n10904]], and Flagship’s Empress is cutting 53% [[n10873]].
Trigger to Watch
A turn in venture funding, and an end to the layoff wave. Both are observable quarter by quarter, and either one would move the theme from cheap to consensus.

crypto.title: Crypto & Digital Assets — bitcoin holds, the rest does not
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 82,718.50 USD, down 1.93% over 20 sessions from 84,347.02 on 2025-02-26, and up 2.04% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-18). Ether is far weaker at 1,932.54 USD, down 17.11% over 20 sessions from 2,331.45 on 2025-02-26. Solana is at 125.31, down 7.06%, and dogecoin is down 18.25%. New / Most Important

Standard Chartered cut its ether forecast for 2025 by 60%, citing increased competition and declining revenue [[n1936]]. That is the most important crypto signal in the window, because it targets the revenue case rather than the price. Canada’s first levered bitcoin and ether ETFs were expected to begin trading on 18 March [[n1891]], and Canary Capital’s filing for a SUI ETF [[n1893]] shows the product pipeline still expanding as prices fall. The ETF pipeline keeps growing even as prices fall: Hashdex wants to add XRP and ADA to its crypto index ETF [[n1842]], and Michael Saylor says bitcoin will rip forward with a vengeance when risk-on returns [[n1826]].
Playbook

Hold bitcoin as the core, and avoid ether and the miners until the trend changes. Reclaiming 84,347.02, the 26 February close, would move the bias from defensive to constructive. Keep size small around the Fed: bitcoin volatility clusters on FOMC days [[n1887]], and a whale’s $368 million short ahead of the decision [[n1821]] shows how levered the positioning is. The call changes if ether reclaims 2,331.45 or if the miners stop making new lows.

flows.title: Capital Flows & Liquidity Framework — duration over equity beta
parts: Global Liquidity

Central banks are easing unevenly. The ECB cut its key rate to 2.5% on 6 March [[n3174]], and the Bank of England is set to keep rates on hold as global uncertainty mounts [[n3348]]. In Asia, the PBOC says it will create more tools to shore up the economy [[n1263]], and a reported US$1 trillion reserves fund in Hong Kong would be a large new liquidity channel [[n1309]]. The Fed is the marginal setter, and markets expect two cuts starting in September [[n11158]]. Global M2 is tightening its grip on bitcoin, one analysis says [[n1765]], which matters for the crypto liquidity channel. Japan’s bond market adds to the picture, with 10-year yields having surged near 16-year highs in early March [[n5057]]. Gold’s central-bank demand is part of the same story, with Luxembourg’s gold reserves topping €200 million [[n9038]].
Rates & Dollar

The 10-year closed at 4.29% and the 2-year at 4.04%, with a positively sloped curve that has moved into bull flattening over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-18). The dollar index is at 103.24 index points, down 3.56% over 20 sessions, while EUR/USD is at 1.0919, up 4.14% over the same window, and USD/JPY is at 149.3790. The dollar is weaker against both the euro and the yen. BNP Paribas says euro strength, not dollar weakness, is the story [[n3419]], and Reuters notes the dollar is not among the big currency winners of 2025 so far [[n3335]]. TLT is up 2.96% over 20 sessions at 90.71 USD, so the duration bid is doing the work.
Credit Check

HYG, the high-yield ETF, closed at 78.93 USD, down 0.95% over 20 sessions, while LQD, the investment-grade ETF, rose 0.82% over the same window to 108.43 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Credit is still open for issuers: BMW is selling $4 billion of bonds as issuers front-load deals [[n3725]], and elite colleges in Trump’s crosshairs are rushing to the bond market at a record pace [[n3746]]. The stress is at the edges. Moody’s cut Romania’s outlook on budget risks [[n3331]], and France’s borrowing costs are near a 14-year high [[n3279]]. S&P Global sets out best practice for risk management in private credit [[n3412]], and Deutsche Bank is giving DWS a first look at its private credit deals [[n8888]].
Equity & Fund Flows

The flow data are the sharpest part of the picture. Bank of America’s survey shows the biggest-ever drop in US equity allocation, which it calls a bull crash [[n3808]], and Business Insider reports investors dumped a record amount of US stock as stagflation fears bit [[n3838]]. Hedge-fund momentum bets cratered all at once in volatile markets [[n3848]], and hedge funds cut their stakes in all of the Magnificent 7 stocks last quarter except one [[n3706]]. Investors still bought the Magnificent 7 ETF amid the downturn [[n6050]]. In China, record gold ETF inflows arrived in February [[n3641]], and foreign inflows into Chinese stocks and EM debt were large [[n1188]].
Portfolio Implication

Own duration and cut equity beta. The 10-year at 4.29% is 26 bps lower over 20 observations and TLT is up 2.96%, so the bond bid is working while the US equity bid is not. Keep an overweight in Europe’s fiscal chain and China’s policy-led equities, trim US high beta into the Fed and the April 2 tariff deadline [[n9154]], and keep gold as the hedge against a weaker dollar. The call changes if high yield stops falling and credit spreads tighten, because that would say the growth scare is ending and the duration bid is premature.

anticipatory.title: Fed decision on March 19 — duration against the growth scare
parts: What Is Priced

Markets expect the Fed to cut twice this year, starting in September [[n11158]], and Nasdaq says options are underpricing the FOMC reaction [[n11297]]. The 10-year at 4.29% and the 2-year at 4.04% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-18) already embed a lot of easing. Morningstar frames Wednesday’s decision as the event to read [[n11159]], and bitcoin traders have sized their positions around the March 19 meeting [[n1821]].
Conditional Expression

If the Fed holds and signals patience, the front end stops rallying and the curve can steepen out of its bull-flattening path. The position is to keep duration and add index hedges. If the Fed leans dovish on growth, the 10-year rallies further, TLT extends its 2.96% gain over 20 sessions, and gold keeps its bid. Either way, US high beta is the piece to trim.
Risk

A hawkish surprise into a stagflation backdrop [[n11419]] would hit both duration and equities, and the VIX at 21.70 would jump. The Wall Street Journal’s framing of a double threat to Powell [[n11390]] is the reminder that political pressure on the Fed is part of the risk.

anticipatory.title: BOJ decision — the yen decides who wins
parts: What Is Priced

Goldman expects the BOJ to hike gradually given the wage outlook [[n5273]], while XTB’s currency note expects the BOJ to hold off on a rate hike [[n5968]]. USD/JPY at 149.3790 sits below the 151.44 level of 18 February (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18), so the market has not yet priced a hawkish turn. FOREX.com still has the BOJ and the FOMC ahead [[n0529]].
Conditional Expression

A hold keeps the yen soft and supports the trading houses. A hike, even a small one, pushes USD/JPY lower and hurts the exporters. The trade is to keep the trading houses and hedge the exporters ahead of the decision.
Risk
A hawkish hold backed by strong wage settlements [[n5149]] would send the yen sharply stronger and the Nikkei lower, and the 2.86% five-session gain in the Nikkei would be at risk.

anticipatory.title: April 2 tariff deadline — autos and the tariff floor
parts: What Is Priced

Stellantis is working with suppliers and dealers ahead of the April 2 tariff deadline [[n9154]], and strategists say the sell-off has further to go as tariff deadlines loom [[n3812]]. Tariffs on lumber and appliances are already in place [[n10830]], so the market is not pricing a tariff-free path.
Conditional Expression

If the deadline is extended, the autos rally and the European premium widens. If the tariffs stick, the European autos and the industrials lose more ground, and housing-linked US names stay under pressure. The trade is to underweight European autos into the deadline and hold US utilities as the defensive offset.
Risk
The European auto ETF is already down 5.10% over 20 sessions, so a relief move could be sharp, and a deal could arrive without warning. Stellantis’s preparations are the signal, not the outcome.

anticipatory.title: Russia–Ukraine talks — the defence premium at risk
parts: What Is Priced

Trump and Putin are expected to speak as the US pushes for a ceasefire, Reuters reports [[n4458]], and Ukraine is buying US LNG while the talks continue [[n5446]]. Rheinmetall’s 55.63% gain over 20 sessions prices a long spending cycle (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18).
Conditional Expression

A ceasefire framework removes part of the defence premium. The trade is to trim European defence into a deal and rotate into European infrastructure and industrials that gain from German spending regardless of the outcome. If talks stall, the premium holds and the rearmament bid keeps widening.
Risk

Germany’s budget change has already passed parliament [[n3425]], which limits the fundamental downside. The multiple is what falls on a ceasefire, not the orders, so the risk is one of valuation rather than earnings. The politics cut both ways: Polish presidential campaigning is hardening positions on Ukraine [[n5441]], which keeps the regional risk premium alive.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — GTC demand at a sell-off price
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia unveiled Blackwell Ultra at its keynote on 18 March [[n3001]], and OpenAI’s first Stargate site will hold up to 400,000 Nvidia chips [[n9101]].
