Mixed. Hold a core position and express the upside with a call spread that runs past the GTC week, which Yahoo Finance dates from 18 to 21 March [[n8551]]. Invalidation is a close below $100, which would mean the event did not stop the de-rating.

catalysts.title: $NFLX — pricing power earns an upgrade
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

An analyst upgraded Netflix on 17 March, citing potential future US price hikes and strong ad growth [[n2912]]. Netflix, Amazon and Peacock are going big on popular YouTubers [[n7838]], which widens the content and ad pool. The thesis is that the subscription moat is pricing power, with advertising as a second engine.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NFLX closed at 929.98, up 3.90% over five sessions but 10.22% lower over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The 20-session reference is 1,035.85. The risk is an ad slowdown, and Axios reports that ad growth is slowing [[n8813]].

Bullish. Buy shares on dips toward 930. Invalidation is any sign that the price increases are being walked back, or a cut to the ad outlook.

catalysts.title: $PEP — poppi buys growth in a defensive tape
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

PepsiCo agreed to acquire the prebiotic soda brand poppi for $1.95 billion [[n10821]], and the company announced the deal on 17 March [[n11303]]. The thesis is that a staples group is buying growth in a category shoppers are moving toward, while the wider consumer is squeezed.
Price Hurdle & Risk

PEP closed at 148.99, down 2.19% over five sessions and up 3.39% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The 20-session reference is 144.10. The risk is food-quality headlines: frozen meals sold at Walmart and Kroger were recalled over contamination [[n8935]].

Bullish. Own the shares near 148.99. Invalidation is a close below the 144.10 reference.

catalysts.title: $AVGO — Google’s chip shift is the risk
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Broadcom fell on a report that Google may work with MediaTek on AI [[n8326]], and The Information reports that Google is taking MediaTek for cheaper AI chips [[n8431]]. TrendForce reports the MediaTek chip will still go into production at TSMC [[n9238]]. The thesis is that the custom-silicon share is contestable, and the report puts Broadcom’s Google work at risk.

AVGO closed at 188.67, down 3.00% in the last session and 17.44% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The 20-session reference is 228.53. The risk is that Broadcom’s 77% AI revenue spike [[n2243]] makes the stock hard to short on fundamentals alone.

Bearish. A put spread below 188.67. Invalidation is confirmation of the Google work or a raised AI-revenue outlook.

catalysts.title: $AAPL — China share loss and AI delays
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Apple’s iPhone sales plunge as Huawei takes the lead in China [[n8292]], and the Wall Street Journal says Apple could stay in the penalty box on AI delays [[n8825]]. Apple also lost a German antitrust fight and faces greater scrutiny [[n8832]]. The thesis is that the growth story is being questioned on two fronts at once.
Price Hurdle & Risk

AAPL closed at 212.69, down 3.69% over five sessions and 13.00% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The 20-session reference is 244.47. Apple has lost nearly $700 billion of market value since its record close [[n8833]]. The risk is a bull case: Evercore expects strong growth through 2029 [[n2966]], which would limit the downside.
Trade Expression
Bearish. A put spread below 212.69. Invalidation is a China iPhone recovery or an AI launch the market accepts.

catalysts.title: $ADBE — a beat that guidance overshadowed
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Adobe beat estimates in its first quarter, but the shares fell as revenue guidance disappointed [[n2680]]. CNBC reports the stock dropped 14% as concerns about AI growth overshadowed better-than-expected results [[n2682]]. The thesis is that a beat without a raised outlook does not re-rate the stock.
Price Hurdle & Risk

ADBE closed at 391.37, down 9.75% over five sessions and 15.67% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The 20-session reference is 464.11. The risk is a rebound on AI product news, and retail mood has already hit rock bottom [[n2680]], which makes a short squeeze possible.
Trade Expression
Bearish. Sell rallies toward the 20-session reference, hedging with a call spread. Invalidation is a raised revenue outlook.

retail.title: D-Wave / QBTS — Nvidia's quantum seal of approval
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story the crowd tells itself has moved from the claim to the endorsement. Nvidia says it will build an accelerated quantum computing research center [[n9081]], and its first-ever Quantum Day puts IonQ's executive chair on a panel with Nvidia's chief executive [[n6432]]. Retail reads a chip giant's entry as proof that quantum computing is a business rather than a laboratory, and the pure plays look like the cheapest way to own that business before the megacaps move in. The number holders tend to watch is the round $10 line. D-Wave closed at 10.80 USD, just above it, and every close above that level looks like the second leg of the breakout that Yahoo Finance already called 'only the beginning' [[n8084]].
What Is Driving It

D-Wave closed at 10.80 USD on March 18, up 100.74% over five sessions and 78.81% over 20 from its 6.04 USD reference of February 18, though it fell 3.40% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The peers did not move with it that day. Rigetti fell 8.06% to 10.26 USD and IonQ fell 9.03% to 22.68 USD, although Rigetti is still up 27.45% over five sessions and IonQ up 21.28% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Rigetti's surge also came with a financing: it announced a US$35M private placement and its shares soared 57% afterwards [[n6271]], the kind of equity raise a rally makes possible. The backdrop is hostile. The S&P 500 closed at 5,614.66 points, down 8.40% over 20 sessions, the Nasdaq 100 is down 12.10% over the same span, and the VIX is at 21.70 points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18).
The Social Signal

The vocabulary has moved from breakthrough to test. Investopedia's headline on March 17 is that D-Wave soared further after its breakthrough claim [[n8364]], and Quartz framed the group as climbing before Nvidia's first 'Quantum Day' [[n6356]]. The sharper questions arrived on March 18. Yahoo Finance asks whether Rigetti is a pump-and-dump stock favoured by hedge funds [[n3857]], and The Motley Fool asks whether D-Wave is still a buy [[n9022]]. The crowd is no longer asking whether quantum is real. It is asking whether the price has run ahead of the story, and the pump question is being asked in the same breath as the buy call.
Historical Analog

The mechanism is familiar: when a leader validates a theme, the validated name moves first and the cheaper peers carry the second leg. The difference is who is doing the validating. A chip leader that sells the hardware a theme needs is a supplier; one that builds its own research centre is a competitor for the same story and the same budgets [[n9081]]. That is why the peers' larger fall on March 18 matters more than D-Wave's rally: the price did not confirm the validation on the day it landed.
Smart Money View

The split is between the company that matters most to the field and the capital moving around it. The supportive case is Nvidia itself, which is building its own quantum research center [[n9081]], and whose technical blog reports that it and QuEra decode quantum errors with AI [[n9077]]. The hedging case is capital. Rigetti's US$35M private placement was followed by a 57% share jump [[n6271]], so management raised equity into the rally. The Motley Fool's question about whether D-Wave is still a buy [[n9022]] shows the buy case is being argued, not assumed. The disagreement is about how fast the commercial timeline arrives, not whether the technology matters.
When the Narrative Breaks

Watch the levels and the calendar. The round $10 line is the first test, and a close below it would turn the 10.80 USD close into a fade. Rigetti rose 27.45% over five sessions yet already sits below its own 20-session reference of 10.52 USD at 10.26 USD, so the peer rally is not confirming the 20-session trend. Nvidia's event runs from March 18 through March 21 [[n8551]], so the panel and the research centre are the observable test: a sell-the-news reaction in those sessions would confirm the break that the March 18 peer fall already hinted at. The instrument risk is dilution. A rally financed by a private placement can gap down when the new shares arrive, and IonQ, at 22.68 USD, sits 33.18% below its 20-session reference of 33.94 USD, which shows how far a pure play can fall when the story pauses.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — shorts are cashing in on the backlash
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The crowd's story has turned from loyalty into a fight. Business Insider's headline on March 18 is that short sellers are making a fortune out of the backlash against Elon Musk [[n3882]], and CBS News reports that Teslas in Las Vegas were set on fire and shot in what police call a targeted attack [[n9162]]. The reading that follows is that the company is being punished for its chief executive's politics, and that the people betting against it are the ones profiting. A discount is a valuation question. A burned car is a grievance, and a grievance is harder to argue away with a forecast.
Where It Breaks

TSLA closed at 225.31 USD on March 18, down 5.34% in the last session and 36.37% over 20 sessions from 354.11 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). The S&P 500 is down 8.40% over the same span, so the stock's fall is not an index effect. The round $200 line is the test. The demand evidence is the new part: Electrek's headline on March 17 says Tesla already offers 0% interest on the new Model Y in China, a sign of weak demand [[n1430]], and Kelley Blue Book reports that US Tesla registrations sank as other EVs rose [[n8576]]. The next registrations print is the trigger, and single-stock beta is the instrument risk.

retail.title: Hims & Hers / HIMS — is the compounded-drug boom over?
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Hims & Hers was the leveraged way into the weight-loss boom. Yahoo Finance reported on March 12 that Defiance launched a 2X leveraged ETF on the telehealth name [[n6030]], so traders could bet on the stock through a daily-reset wrapper. The crowd's story is that millions of patients want cheap access to weight-loss treatment, and compounded versions of the drugs are the cheap route. A March 14 headline says the compounded drugs that millions of people take are about to disappear [[n7909]]. The story assumed that route stayed open.
Where It Breaks

HIMS closed at 31.49 USD on March 18, down 9.22% in the last session and 9.28% over five sessions, and it is down 46.17% over 20 sessions from 58.50 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Quartz's headline says the stock tumbled as the FDA issued a warning about 'unapproved' weight-loss drugs [[n6425]], which is the regulatory break. The round $30 line is next, and a close below it would extend the slide. Inquirer.com reported on March 17 that insurers are cutting coverage for weight-loss drugs [[n8609]]. The instrument risk is the 2X wrapper, which resets daily, so it multiplies each day's move rather than the slide over 20 sessions.

retail.title: Gold / GLD — the record while bitcoin falls
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Gold is the trade that sits next to a falling bitcoin. Decrypt's headline on March 18 is that gold set a new all-time high while bitcoin is falling [[n1908]], and CNBC TV18 reports that gold hit an all-time high for the second time within a week [[n8965]]. Barron's headline says it is gold's time to shine as the stock market slump continues [[n11408]], and vietnamnews.vn reports that experts warn of FOMO amid soaring gold prices [[n6416]]. The story is a fear trade with a record attached, and the record gives the crowd a number to chase.
Where It Breaks

Gold futures closed at 3,040.80 USD on March 18, up 4.10% over five sessions and 3.11% over 20 from 2,949.00 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-18). Bitcoin closed at 82,718.50 USD, down 1.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-18). The round $3,000 line is the test: a Yahoo Finance UK headline says gold hit a record of over $3,000 [[n8959]], and a close back under it would end the run. The Fed meets on March 19 [[n1821]], and a firmer dollar is the risk, although the dollar index is already down 3.56% over 20 sessions. GLD tracks bullion one-for-one, so the ETF carries the full drop if the record fails.
